newsitem.title: UK: Broad EMU expectations consolidate-JP Morgan index.
newsitem.headline: Broad EMU expectations consolidate-JP Morgan index.

text.p: Market expectations of a broad-based European monetary union stagnated and even reversed in the case of Spain after two weeks of strong gains, according to JP Morgan's EMU calculator.
"EMU expecations were apparently influenced more by the anticipation of a stability pact than its reality," said JP Morgan currency research team in London.
European Union leaders agreed an EMU stability pact in Dublin on December 13.

JP Morgan's EMU calculator, which gauges the probability of individual countries joing EMU in 1999 by financial market prices, showed Spain's probability decreasing by six percentage points to 78 percent in the past five-day trading period. However, Spain was still up 16 points over the last 20 trading days.
Elsewhere, EMU probabilities of Italy and Denmark also dipped slightly with Italy slipping two points to 68 percent and Denmark down one point to 45 percent in the past week.
Probability levels for Sweden bucked the trend and made a three point gain to 77 percent while the UK was unchanged at 39 percent.
According to these calculations, the market still believes there is a 100 percent chance of France and Belgium will be in EMU and that was unchanged from last week.

The calculator works by assigning a market probability level to each country. This is derived from the actual swap spread, an in-house assumption of what the spread would be if EMU were not a factor and the expected spread after EMU participation, which is zero.
